content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to record data with a [product_name] onto an SD card or directly to a computer? My issue is as follows: I'll be using a sensor with a [product_name]. The system will track products at a certain rate (e.g., 30 products per minute). I want to monitor uptime, downtime, product rate, etc., and store this information. Example: Uptime - 13:10 0 units Downtime - 15:00 1500 units Uptime - 15:10 1500 units Downtime - 16:40 3300 units ...and so on Thanks! [user_name]

You can transfer recorded data from the SD card to a computer as a CSV file. Just connect your PC to the Ethernet interface, then use [product_name] software and choose "Upload datalog" from the Tools → Transfer menu. To record data, activate the datalog feature in [product_name] software and set it to 'enabled' whenever you wish to log information. Within the datalog setup, you can select which logic block's data should be captured. In your situation: a transition from low to high for uptime would enable datalogging. The function will record the output from a counter linked to your sensor.
Thank you! I'll start creating my program next week. I'll return if I encounter any issues. Thanks for your quick response.

The focus is on easy access to relevant information, flexible data selection, and straightforward transfer and retrieval, with no major difficulties mentioned.
